assertions.description: document.requestStorageAccessFor is no longer exposed — the Chrome 153 'Removal of APIs' rollout step (deprecated since Chrome 144). Fails honestly on installs the stepped rollout has not reached.
document.requestStorageAccess (the core Storage Access API) is still available — only the 'For' variant is removed.
document.hasStorageAccess remains as the parallel introspection method.
A top-level, first-party document reports hasStorageAccess() === true — the removal does not disturb first-party access semantics.
navigator.permissions.query({name:'storage-access'}) still resolves — the Permissions surface for the parent API is preserved.
The 'top-level-storage-access' permission name (only used by requestStorageAccessFor) rejects when queried once the removal has landed.
